main_body: A flat ground patch of dark olive-green grass/moss tiling, repeating a 16px tile pattern with scattered light-green blades, dark clumps, and small yellow and red flower dots
top_band: none (terrain ground tile; no standing object, only a repeating flat texture of one dark green base with dot details)
evidence: The candidate is a terrain ground patch, not a standing object, so the 3/4 top/front-face contract does not apply. The column scan shows a uniform base (L=65) with a repeating 3-row blade/shadow motif every 16 rows, which is normal ground texture and has no object body to fail.

style.evidence: The candidate has 12 distinct colours and a median of 12 per tile, which is at or above the paving reference (7) but well under the grass reference (26 per tile, 80 colours in total). It has no 5x5 flat-fill blocks (0%), and the dark pixels are tinted green-brown (0% neutral), so there is no sticker outline. The base is one dark green (L=65) with sparse blade clumps and flower dots, so shading is limited to about 4 steps against the grass reference's 5-6. The tile repeats an identical 16px motif, which reads as mechanical and thinner than the reference's varied grass tufts. A careful artist would likely find it flatter and lower in variation than the grass reference, so it fails.
